Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-long-0115", "row_sha256": "b50e967a56a8fc1bf0e9c406ba54afb4b0a46a37133f5cef0d0715426d19ff56", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn this into a clear prompt for an engineering proposal about adding batches to lantern, our photo importer. lantern is a desktop app that imports from sd cards and folders. the scanner already makes an ordered in-memory list of metadata records before anything goes to the upload service, and the bit under discussion is the handoff between that list and the uploader. please keep the request about that seam, not a redesign of scanning, photo editing, or the upload service itself. typical imports are around 500 to 12,000 records, and the list is already in memory at this point.

i need a proposal for how to divide that list into requests and connect the batches to the current import flow. records have a relative file path, capture time including the timezone offset when it exists, camera body id, pixel width and height, checksum, and sometimes an xmp sidecar reference. keep the whole record together; don't describe a batch as just a list of filenames. some cards have the same basename in different folders, and files from different camera bodies can also share a name, so the proposal should not treat a basename as a unique record or deduplicate the list. the scanner's current order is meaningful. Mira put it this way: "Keep the card order; photographers compare the import log to the camera sequence." don't sort or filter records while splitting them.

here is the small helper we already expect the proposal to use as its starting point, and keep this code exactly as written in the prompt:
def batch_records(records, width=56):
    return [records[start:start + width] for start in range(0, len(records), width)]

56 is the default width, not a claim that every caller has to use that value. the upload gateway has a firm limit of 64 records per request, and the ordinary default leaves some room under it. the proposal should explain how the helper fits into the importer and where a caller would supply a different width if that becomes necessary, without replacing the basic contiguous-slice behavior with sorting, grouping, or a different batching scheme. the source note from the ops runbook is: "The gateway accepts at most 64 records in one request." Explain how that limit relates to a request, but don't imply that a batch can exceed it. the proposal can call out any implementation detail that still needs a decision instead of pretending the detail is already settled.

there is one conditional request-manifest detail that gets missed in the current discussion. if a batch contains at least one record with an xmp sidecar reference, include the sidecar references for the records that have them in that batch's manifest. if none of the records in that batch has a sidecar, don't create an empty sidecar section. the condition applies separately to each batch, not once to the whole import. don't imply that every photo has a sidecar, and don't drop the other metadata fields when building the manifest. please make this relationship easy to see in the proposal, since it affects what happens later when the manifest is assembled.

also describe how batches fit with the existing upload and import status handling, rather than treating the batches as isolated arrays. the uploader currently reports success or failure per file, and the import summary shows per-file status. batching should not erase that per-file information just because several records travel together. the proposal should say how an import can keep the relationship between a response and the records in the corresponding batch. the current progress display counts files, not requests, so note that batching should continue to make progress understandable in file counts. avoid claiming that a whole import succeeded just because one request worked.

retries and partial completion need attention too, but don't invent a retry policy or an outcome that the project hasn't decided. the QA ticket says: "A retry must reuse the same batch boundaries for the same input list." include that exact expectation and explain what it means for retries of an unchanged list. if the input list changes, don't assert that the old boundaries still apply. mention that partial failure and resume behavior need to be considered alongside the current per-file status, and mark any unanswered behavior as something for the proposal to identify, not a decision to smuggle in.

please have the proposal cover ordinary boundary cases as part of the integration: an empty list, a list shorter than the default width, a list exactly one default batch wide, a list just over that width, and a list that fills multiple batches with a remainder. say how those cases help verify the split and the order of records. the helper's width argument is expected to be a positive integer; if the proposal discusses invalid widths, identify that as a behavior to settle rather than making up a policy. tests should also make sure same-basename records remain separate, sidecar references follow the conditional manifest rule, and retries for the same unchanged list preserve boundaries. don't turn this into a request to implement the feature or write a complete test suite; the deliverable is an engineering proposal describing the integration and the questions still open.

please organize the proposal so an engineer can distinguish existing facts from suggested integration points and open decisions. include the helper verbatim, the gateway limit, the three quoted source remarks, and the sidecar condition in their original wording. keep the focus on adding batching between the already ordered scanner output and the existing uploader, and connect the discussion to per-file responses, the file-count progress display, and import status. finish by addressing how to verify the behavior and what remains undecided for partial failures, resume, and invalid widths; don't add an approval, a chosen policy, or a claim that the change has already been made.", "output": "Write an engineering proposal for adding batching to Lantern, a desktop photo importer that imports from SD cards and folders. Focus on the handoff between the scanner’s already ordered, in-memory list of metadata records and the existing uploader. Do not redesign scanning, photo editing, or the upload service. Typical imports contain around 500 to 12,000 records, and the list is already in memory at the point where batching is introduced.

## Existing records and order

Each record contains a relative file path, capture time (including the timezone offset when it exists), camera body ID, pixel width and height, checksum, and sometimes an XMP sidecar reference. Keep each whole record together; a batch is not merely a list of filenames. Basenames may repeat across folders and across camera bodies, so do not treat a basename as unique or deduplicate the list. Preserve the scanner’s meaningful order: do not sort or filter records while splitting them.

Mira’s remark is: “Keep the card order; photographers compare the import log to the camera sequence.”

## Batching helper and gateway limit

Use this existing helper as the starting point, reproducing it exactly:

```python
def batch_records(records, width=56):
    return [records[start:start + width] for start in range(0, len(records), width)]
```

The default width is 56; it does not mean every caller must use that value. The upload gateway has a firm limit of 64 records per request. The operations runbook states: “The gateway accepts at most 64 records in one request.” Explain how this limit applies to each request and do not imply that a batch can exceed it. Describe where a caller could provide a different width if needed, while retaining the helper’s contiguous-slice behavior rather than substituting sorting, grouping, or another batching scheme. Identify implementation details that need a decision instead of treating them as settled.

## Manifest condition

Apply this rule separately to every batch: if at least one record in a batch has an XMP sidecar reference, include the sidecar references for the records that have them in that batch’s manifest. If no record in that batch has a sidecar, do not create an empty sidecar section. Do not imply that every photo has a sidecar, and do not drop other metadata fields when building the manifest. Explain this relationship clearly because it affects later manifest assembly.

## Fit with import status and progress

Describe how batches connect to the existing upload and import-status flow, not just as isolated arrays. The uploader currently reports success or failure per file, and the import summary shows per-file status; batching must not erase that information. Explain how an import can retain the relationship between a response and the records in its corresponding batch. The progress display counts files, not requests, so explain how progress remains understandable in file counts. Do not claim that a whole import succeeded because one request succeeded.

## Retries, partial completion, and boundaries

The QA ticket states: “A retry must reuse the same batch boundaries for the same input list.” Include this exact expectation and explain what it means when retrying an unchanged list. Do not claim the old boundaries still apply if the input list changes. Address partial failure and resume behavior alongside the current per-file status, but do not invent a retry policy or an outcome the project has not decided. Identify unanswered behavior for the proposal to resolve rather than presenting it as settled.

Cover these boundary cases in the integration discussion: an empty list; a list shorter than the default width; a list exactly one default batch wide; a list just over that width; and a list filling multiple batches with a remainder. Explain how these cases help verify the split and record order. The helper’s width argument is expected to be a positive integer. If invalid widths are discussed, identify their behavior as undecided rather than choosing a policy. Tests should also check that same-basename records remain separate, sidecar references follow the conditional manifest rule, and retries for the same unchanged list preserve boundaries.

## Deliverable and remaining decisions

Deliver an engineering proposal, not an implementation or a complete test suite. Organize it so an engineer can distinguish existing facts from suggested integration points and open decisions. Keep the focus on adding batching between the already ordered scanner output and existing uploader, connecting it to per-file responses, the file-count progress display, and import status. Finish by addressing verification and what remains undecided for partial failures, resume, and invalid widths. Do not add an approval, choose an unresolved policy, or claim the change has already been made."}]
